text:
\(\operatorname{tp}\) assigns a type to every nonlogical symbol.  The sets
\(\mathsf{Sort}\), \(\mathcal F\), and \(\mathcal R\) may have any
cardinality.  Each sort has a countably infinite variable stock.  The variable
form of the reduction below fixes one injection of the disjoint union of the
stocks into the countable first-order variable supply, which exists exactly
when the sorted variables are countable, for instance when \(\mathsf{Sort}\)
is at most countable; the cardinality of \(\mathcal F\) and \(\mathcal R\)
plays no role (\cref{thm:p02-w02b-p02-033-variable-form}).  With uncountably
many sorts no such injection exists, and the reduction takes the parameter
form of \cref{thm:p02-w02b-p02-033-reduction}
(\cref{thm:p02-w02b-p02-033-no-renaming}).

This replaces the restriction with a statement of where each form applies.
